title: Free event Friday will transform DSM's oldest neighborhood into the most haunted

content:
DES MOINES, Iowa --The public is invited to walk the streets of the most historic homes in Des Moines on Friday from 6:30 to 8 p.m., filled with live entertainment, spooky sites, and a giving spirit.

Sherman Hill is celebrating 15 years of Halloween on the Hill, the tradition of transforming Des Moines oldest neighborhood into the scariest.

Organizer Ryan Howell said it's hard to describe.

"You just have to come see it. We close down the streets in Sherman Hill and become sort of a neighborhood-wide haunted house. But it's not just the spooky old Victorian houses that are decorated. We have live actors, we have performers, we have dancers," he said.

 One last walk through Valley West Mall 

Halloween on the Hill was started by a few neighbors in the Sherman Hill area who wanted to celebrate the holiday with decorations and giving back.

"They didn't want to go through all the work just to show it off for one night and not really maybe maximize the benefit for the community," Howell said.

They partnered with the DMARC, Des Moines Area Religious Council food pantry, to help people in central Iowa.

"Right from the start, we said we encourage folks to bring food items so they can contribute to the pantry," Howell said.

The event is free, but donations are encouraged. Click this link to donate online.

He said they brought in 7,000 food items last year and raised almost $25,000, but this year they are hoping to bring in more money to help those in need.

"The money goes a lot further to buy food for folks in our community who need it," he said.

What you need to know

  • 6:30 pm - 8 pm

  • Parking is available at UnityPoint, but please do not park at the Ronald McDonald House

  • Hot chocolate and cider outside of Mickle Center is available for purchase; proceeds go to non-profits
